chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the description of the crowd:
These are the people who, when they assemble together, are overwhelming but when they disperse they cannot be recognized.

key_terms.الْغَوْغَاءِ: The crowd, mob, or people in a state of commotion

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and characteristic of the ghawgha (crowd) in Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes the 'ghawgha' as a volatile social force whose power lies in collective momentum rather than individual conviction, making them formidable in assembly but elusive in isolation. This description reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of mob psychology, where the loss of individual accountability amplifies their capacity for disruption. The insight serves as a practical warning for leaders to manage public sentiment by addressing the collective identity before it fragments.
